industries.narrative: Biotech shows explosive 2.5x rel volume with cap-weighted +1.52% — large-cap leaders VRTX/REGN/ALNY drawing institutional flow on heavy conviction.
Big Pharma nearly universal advance (9/10 up) with solid +1.46% cap-weighted, but rel volume is anemic — defensive rotation, not conviction buying.

sector_breadth_notes.note: Healthcare strength is entirely biotech + big pharma driven. Biotech has volume conviction; pharma has broad breadth. No other healthcare industries qualified.
Industrials qualified at sector level but ZERO industries scored above 6.5 — Specialty Machinery, Electrical Equipment, and Distribution all deeply weak. Sector move is hollow.
Materials sector strength is not confirmed at industry level — Building Materials and Industrial Metals & Mining are among the worst laggards. Suspicious sector-level move.
Financials qualified but Credit Services and Shell Companies are bottom-tier laggards. No financial industry cleared the 6.5 gate — narrow banks-only move likely.
Discretionary shows Lodging and Furnishings as major laggards with no qualifying industries — sector strength is concentrated in mega-caps not captured here.
Utilities qualified but Independent Power Producers are a deep laggard; no utility industry cleared the gate — regulated utilities likely carrying the sector defensively.
Staples qualified at sector level but no industries scored above 6.5 — classic defensive bid without industry-level conviction.

key_divergences: Major divergence: 7 sectors qualified but only Healthcare produced qualifying industries. Cyclicals (XLI, XLB, XLY) show sector-ETF strength while underlying industries deteriorate — suggests mega-cap or ETF-flow-driven moves, not organic breadth.
leadership_theme: Defensive rotation: biotech conviction + big pharma breadth; cyclicals hollow underneath
